title: setup.py --check: C6 installed-file drift detection
problem: setup.py installs files from the repo into ~/.claude/ (slash commands, skills, hook configs). Today --check verifies that target files exist but never compares content: a user who edits the installed copy (or a dev who edits the repo copy without re-running setup.py) creates silent drift between what's installed and what's under version control. This is a class C6 failure mode (installation integrity) with no current detection; problems surface only when behavior diverges from expectation and someone debugs far enough to notice the file contents differ.
description: Extend setup.py run_check() with a drift-detection pass. For each file setup.py installs, compute sha256 of the installed copy in ~/.claude/ and sha256 of the source copy in the repo, and fail(msg) with both paths if they differ. Enumerate the installed set from the existing install functions (install_commands, register_hooks, skill install paths) — do not re-scan ~/.claude/ from scratch. Skip files that are missing from the installed side (the existing --check already catches those elsewhere). Print ok() per file that matches, fail() per file that drifts. Detect-only for this ticket; auto-repair is explicitly out of scope.
scope: setup.py (run_check body + a sha256 helper, stdlib hashlib). New test file core/test_setup_check.py covering: (a) fresh install shows 0 drift; (b) editing any installed command/skill/hook target file reports it drifted with both paths; (c) reverting the edit shows clean again; (d) missing installed file is NOT reported as drifted (existing check handles it). No changes to install_commands/register_hooks/skill install paths themselves. stdlib only.
context: Parent is T-2026-1 (Poetry migration); this ticket splits out the drift-detection portion which is the runner-ready sub-scope with clear acceptance. The Poetry portion stays on T-1. The existing run_check() in setup.py already handles presence checks (file exists / symlink correct); this PR only adds content-integrity checks on files that are present. Chosen as the first chained-executor debut in session 51082b1a because blast radius is tiny (setup.py runs only at install time) and acceptance is deterministic (sha256 compare).
